description: The only dependency bot on this repository. It owns both version and security
updates for all three things that reach production: the npm tree, the GitHub Actions
the workflows run, and the Dockerfile base-image digest.
Dependabot is gone entirely — its version updates were redundant with this file, and
keeping its security updates meant keeping a pull_request_target workflow that held
contents: write and pull-requests: write in order to auto-merge them. Removing a
privileged workflow is worth more than the integration was.
Turn Dependabot security updates OFF in the repository settings (Settings → Code
security). Left on, they duplicate every PR vulnerabilityAlerts below opens, and

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security updates, and the one path that ignores the schedule and the release-age hold above — a known-exploitable version is not something to sit on until Monday, and the hold exists to slow unvetted *new* releases rather than fixes for old ones. Still never automerged: a security fix is frequently a minor or major bump, which is exactly the shape this repository reviews by hand. osvVulnerabilityAlerts widens detection beyond GitHub's own advisories, and transitiveRemediation lets a fix land as a lockfile-only bump when the vulnerable package is not a direct dependency.

lockFileMaintenance.description: A lockfile refresh moves the whole transitive tree in one PR with no upstream release to read. Transitive updates arrive with the direct update that pulls them.

packageRules.description: Keep npm versions exact. package.json pins every dependency to a single version deliberately: with financial credentials in this image, an upgrade should be a reviewed commit rather than a range that resolves differently on the next install.

Let a new npm release sit for three days before it is offered. The npm supply-chain pattern this defends against is a compromised release that is published, installed by whatever updates within the hour, and yanked the same day. Dependabot has no equivalent control.
Group non-breaking npm updates by dependency type, and every major on its own, mirroring the grouping dependabot.yml used.
Development dependencies, grouped separately: they do not ship in the image.

The only automerge in this config, and the same policy the removed dependabot-auto-merge.yml workflow enforced: a patch update to a direct npm dependency, nothing else. platformAutomerge hands the merge to GitHub, so the required lint, test and security checks still have to pass first — and it needs no workflow and no elevated token, which is why that workflow could go.

Actions and the base image are never automerged, and the rule is stated rather than left implicit. Neither reaches production through the application's dependency tree: action code runs in CI with that job's scopes, including the job holding the registry credentials that publish :latest, and the digest *is* the deployed artifact. Placed after the npm rule so it cannot be overridden by it.
GitHub Actions. Renovate updates a pinned SHA and its trailing version comment together, which is the part that is easy to get wrong by hand.

The Dockerfile base image, pinned by digest. This is the only thing that refreshes that pin, and the digest carries the kernel-adjacent libraries as well as Node itself. The comment above the FROM line records which Node and Alpine versions the digest resolved to and when — re-resolve those when reviewing the PR; the command is in the Dockerfile.
Node itself, from .nvmrc and package.json engines. A floor bump changes what CI tests and what the image runs, so it is reviewed on its own rather than grouped with anything.
Every major on its own PR, in every ecosystem.
